problem: Prior semantic/target navigation either builds a metric/semantic 3D map ahead of time and then plans, which needs reliable localization and ignores contextual semantics, or learns end-to-end from raw pixels, which generalizes poorly to unseen homes. Raw-pixel policies also cannot be trained jointly on simulated and real data without domain adaptation or randomization.
motivation: A robot told 'go to the refrigerator' in an unexplored home must use contextual cues, such as which objects co-occur where, rather than a pre-built map. Off-the-shelf detectors and segmenters already capture scene layout, obstacles and target locations. In simulation the same masks can be rendered exactly from labels, so these outputs could be an equitable representation across the sim and real domains.
key_idea: Replace raw RGB with semantic segmentation and object-detection masks from off-the-shelf models (rendered as ground truth in SUNCG), and train an LSTM policy to regress the shortest-path 'progress' cost of every action. This allows joint real + synthetic training with no domain adaptation.
insight: Semantic masks (Det, SSeg) are lossy compared with RGB but generalize better to entirely different homes. The ResNet-50 RGB embedding does better only on the 'similar environments' split, i.e. it overfits to seen homes. Because the masks look the same in sim and real, adding SUNCG data improves Det/SSeg and their combination, sometimes by over 10%, while raw Depth gets worse because of the Kinect-vs-perfect-depth reality gap. Other ablations (bar figures only): (1) removing recurrence sharply lowers success and causes oscillation, and more data does not fix it; (2) dropping the COCO 'Furniture' superclass hurts most, because large furniture is visible from far away and predicts location; (3) dropping 'Food' barely matters.
method: Semantic visual representations: Det is an H×W×80 stack of filled 0/1 box masks per COCO class from Faster R-CNN. SSeg is an H×W×C mask stack from a NYUv2-trained segmenter (Mousavian et al. 3DV'16). Depth has 2 channels: normalized depth plus a validity mask. RGB uses ResNet-50 features. In SUNCG, masks and boxes come from ground-truth labels and the renderer.

Per-modality encoder: 3 conv layers (8×8×8 stride 4, 4×4×16 stride 2, 3×3×16 stride 1) followed by an FC layer giving a 128-d embedding per modality. Inputs are resized to 64×64; RGB instead goes through a 299×299 ResNet-50.

Policy network: the one-hot target class is projected to 128-d and concatenated with the modality embeddings, the previous action and a binary collision indicator. This passes through 2048-d FC layers and a 2048-d LSTM, which outputs a cost v(o,a;c) for each action.

Progress-cost supervision: the target y(s,a;c) is the expected change in shortest-path distance to the goal after action a, in [-1,1] on the known training graph. Collisions are set to +2; stop is -2 at the goal and +2 elsewhere. The loss is MSE over all state-action pairs, which handles cases where several actions are optimal (unlike behavioral cloning or DAgger).
Controller: at test time the agent takes argmin_a v(o,a;c); history is modeled implicitly by the LSTM.

Sim+real joint training: each episode is sampled uniformly from AVD or 200 SUNCG houses (House3D subset) with matched camera parameters, height and step size. Simulated depth is corrupted to mimic Kinect: clipped at 12 m, scaled by U[0.9,1.1], 10% of values dropped. Training uses 8 trajectories × 20 steps per batch, Adam at lr 1e-4, 200k iterations on 40 GPUs (16 h).

setting.backbone: Small CNN encoders + 2048-d LSTM trained from scratch, on top of frozen Faster R-CNN (COCO) detections and a NYUv2-trained semantic segmenter; ResNet-50 (ImageNet) for the RGB variant
setting.training_data: Active Vision Dataset training scans (real, dense image scans of homes) plus 200 SUNCG synthetic houses (House3D subset) with ground-truth masks; supervision from shortest paths on the known environment graph
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D, converted to detection masks + semantic segmentation masks (+ optional depth / RGB features), plus previous action and a collision flag
setting.action_space: discrete {move_forward, move_back, move_left, move_right, rotate_cw, rotate_ccw, stop} on the AVD image lattice
setting.simulator: Active Vision Dataset (real image-based navigation graph) + SUNCG rendering for training
setting.privileged: none for the learned policy (it assumes a collision-detection signal is available as input)

numbers.method: Ours (semantic representation + LSTM, trained on AVD + SUNCG; exact modality combination not stated in text)
numbers.backbone: Faster R-CNN/NYUv2 segmenter masks + CNN-LSTM policy
numbers.extra: 'different environments' split (unseen homes); 5 target categories; success = within 5 steps of any goal instance; max 100 steps; trained with extra SUNCG synthetic data
numbers.evidence: Abstract: 'Our approach successfully gets to the target in $54\%$ of the cases in unexplored environments, compared to $46\%$ for a non-learning based approach, and $28\%$ for a learning-based baseline.'

numbers_note: All ablation results (RGB vs Det/SSeg/Depth, similar vs different environments, AVD-only vs AVD+SUNCG, feedforward vs LSTM, COCO superclass removal) appear only in bar charts (Figs. 3-6) with no numeric values in the text. Only the headline 54% is printed. The text does not say which exact modality combination gives 54%, nor what the 28% learning-based baseline is.
results: On unseen homes in the Active Vision Dataset, the learned semantic-representation policy reaches the target 54% of the time. The strongest baseline, at 46%, is a semi-random search baseline that is given the full environment graph, global poses, depth and a detector. A learning-based baseline reaches 28%. Adding SUNCG synthetic data improves the Det/SSeg models (sometimes by more than 10%) without domain adaptation, but hurts the Depth-based model.
limitations: Evaluation covers only 9 real AVD homes, a discrete image lattice and 5 target categories, with a lenient 5-step success radius. There is no physical robot deployment.
Most quantitative results are shown only in bar charts; the exact configuration behind the 54% headline and the learning baseline are not specified.
Performance depends on external detector and segmenter quality. Raw depth suffers a sim-to-real gap that the representation does not solve.
compares_to: Semi-random search baseline with GT graph/pose + object detector
Learning-based baseline (end-to-end ResNet-50 RGB policy, presumably)
